name: RES4SHO linear two-stage schedule
plain: The baseline of the family: pivot and slope are ignored and each stage is a straight line in sigma. About 60% of the steps go linearly from σ_max to the linear midpoint and the rest from the midpoint to σ_min, then a final step to 0. Not the same as other packs' 'linear' schedulers, which are usually one straight line. Surprises shared by the whole family: a request for N steps returns N+1 steps (n = N+2 minus one junction value, plus a trailing 0); the split point is the linear midpoint of σ_max..σ_min with 60% of the steps above it, so on SD-style models (σ_max about 14.6) most steps sit above σ≈7.3; slopes are divided by n/40, so the shape changes with step count. Registered with use_ms=True; names already in the scheduler table are skipped, not overwritten.
math:
Symbols: N requested steps; σ_max, σ_min from the model; n = N + 2; m = int(0.6 n); σ_mid = σ_min + 0.5(σ_max − σ_min) (linear midpoint).
Stage 1: k = 0..m−1, pivot p1 = m, slope s1' = s1/max(n/40, 0.1); Stage 2: k = 0..n−m−1, pivot p2 = 0, slope s2' = s2/max(n/40, 0.1).
Each stage: r_k = curve(k; p, s'); r̂_k = (r_k − r_last)/(r_first − r_last); σ_k = end + r̂_k (start − end), stage 1 from σ_max to σ_mid, stage 2 from σ_mid to σ_min.
Output = stage 1 without its last value, stage 2, then 0: N+2 values, i.e. N+1 steps.
curve(k) = linspace(1, 0, len) per stage, so σ is piecewise linear with a kink at σ_mid after m−1 steps.

props.prints: draws an ASCII plot of the schedule to the console on every call
